## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- At fixed context, the model produces a distribution $p$ over the vocabulary. Its entropy $H(p)=-\sum_i p_i\log p_i$ is the average surprisal under that distribution.
- On the same vocabulary, a uniform distribution has maximum entropy. A distribution concentrated on a single token has zero entropy.
- For an observed token $y$, surprisal is $-\log p(y)$. The smaller the probability the model assigns to $y$, the greater its surprisal.
- The natural logarithm gives nats. The base-2 logarithm gives bits.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

Given the same context, two models assign probabilities to two tokens. The first assigns 90% and 10%, the second 50% and 50%. Which distribution has higher entropy? What is the second token’s surprisal under the first model if it is observed?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

The uniform distribution has higher entropy, $\log 2\approx 0.693$ nats. The second token has probability $0.1$ under the first model, so its surprisal is $-\log 0.1\approx 2.303$ nats.

</details>
